newsitem.title: UK: Eastern Europe attractive for insurers - report.
newsitem.headline: Eastern Europe attractive for insurers - report.

text.p: Prospects for insurers in eastern Europe are generally positive, but the situation differs considerably from one country to another, UK based management consultant Datamonitor said on Monday.

"Overall, the Eastern European insurance market shows promise. Over the period 1993 to 1996 total insurance penetration in the region grew at a rate of over 5.0 percent each year," it said in its latest Global Insurance report.
Slovenia, the Czech Republic, Poland and Russia have the strongest growth rates, with the first two being driven by general insurance and the latter two by life insurance.

Slovakia also has rapidly expanding personal motor and household insurance markets. Growth rates in Slovakia, the Czech Republic and Slovenia were around 10-25 percent in the years 1991-1996 and Datamonitor sees this continuing.
In Poland and Russia, life insurance sales have been growing at an average 60 percent a year after inflation.
"This is phenomenal growth given the comparative sluggishness of the general economic development."
The region's underperformers between 1993 and 1996 were Croatia, Bulgaria, Romania and Hungary, but Datamonitor believes that the countries with the lowest penetration have high scope for growth.
